h1: Discount Calculator — Percent Off & Stacked Deals
description: Enter any original price and one or two discount percentages. Get the exact final price, how much you save, and the real combined rate when two discounts stack (it's never the simple sum).
answerSnippet: To calculate a discount: multiply the original price by (1 − discount/100). Example: $150 at 30% off → $150 × 0.70 = **$105** (you save $45). For stacked discounts (e.g. 20% + 10%), the real combined rate is 28%, not 30% — because the second discount applies to the already-reduced price: (1 − 0.20) × (1 − 0.10) = 0.72, so you pay 72% of the original.
intro: A **20% + 10%** sticker doesn't mean 30% off — the second discount applies to the already-reduced price, so the real saving is **28%**. Enter your price and one or two percentages; this calculator gives the exact final price, dollar savings, and the true combined rate instantly.
keyTakeaway: A $100 item at 20% off costs $80 (save $20). Stack an extra 10% and you pay $72 — a real **28% discount**, not 30%. The combined rate is always less than the sum of the parts.

explanation:
## How to Calculate a Percent Discount

The formula is: **Final Price = Original Price × (1 − discount / 100)**. Savings = Original Price − Final Price.

| Original Price | Discount | Final Price | You Save |
|---|---|---|---|
| $50 | 10% | $45.00 | $5.00 |
| $100 | 20% | $80.00 | $20.00 |
| $100 | 25% | $75.00 | $25.00 |
| $200 | 30% | $140.00 | $60.00 |
| $300 | 40% | $180.00 | $120.00 |
| $500 | 50% | $250.00 | $250.00 |
| $80 | 15% | $68.00 | $12.00 |
| $120 | 33% | $80.40 | $39.60 |

## How Stacked Discounts Work

When two discounts apply one after the other, each is computed on the new lower base — they do **not** simply add:

```
factor      = (1 - d1/100) × (1 - d2/100)
finalPrice  = originalPrice × factor
savings     = originalPrice - finalPrice
realPercent = savings / originalPrice × 100
```

**Combined rate shortcut:** `d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2) / 100`
For 20% and 10%: 20 + 10 − (20 × 10)/100 = 30 − 2 = **28%**.

## Common Stacked Discount Examples

| First Discount | Second Discount | Combined Real Rate |
|---|---|---|
| 10% | 10% | 19% |
| 20% | 10% | 28% |
| 25% | 15% | 36.25% |
| 30% | 20% | 44% |
| 50% | 50% | 75% |
| 20% | 20% | 36% |
| 15% | 5% | 19.25% |

## Worked Example — Stacked Discounts

**$120 item: 25% sale, then extra 15% coupon**

| Step | Calculation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| After 25% off | $120 × 0.75 | $90.00 |
| After 15% coupon | $90 × 0.85 | **$76.50** |
| Savings | $120 − $76.50 | **$43.50** |
| Real discount | 43.50 / 120 × 100 | **36.25%** (not 40%) |

## Does Order Matter?

For two **percentage** discounts: no. 20% then 10% gives the same final price as 10% then 20% (multiplication is commutative). Order only matters when mixing a percentage discount with a fixed-dollar coupon.

## What This Calculator Does Not Cover

- **Sales tax** — applied after discounts at checkout; this shows the pre-tax final price.
- **Buy One Get One (BOGO)** — treat as 50% off one item's price if needed.
- **Fixed-dollar coupons** — subtract the coupon first, then apply the percentage discount.

faq.q: How do I calculate percent off?
faq.a: Multiply the original price by (1 − discount/100). For 25% off $80: $80 × 0.75 = $60. Savings = $80 − $60 = $20. This calculator handles it instantly.
No. The second discount applies to the price already reduced by the first. The real combined rate is 28%, not 30%. The formula: d1 + d2 − (d1×d2)/100 = 20 + 10 − 2 = 28%.

faq.q: How do I find the original price from the sale price?
faq.a: Divide the sale price by (1 − discount/100). If an item sells for $63 after a 30% discount, the original was $63 ÷ 0.70 = $90.

faq.q: Does the order of two stacked discounts change the final price?
faq.a: Not for two percentage discounts — multiplication is commutative, so 20% then 10% gives the same result as 10% then 20%. Order does matter if one coupon is a fixed dollar amount.
$120 × 0.50 = $60. You pay $60 and save $60. Stack an additional 10% and you pay $54 (a real 55% combined discount).

faq.q: How do I calculate three stacked discounts?
faq.a: Multiply all (1 − rate) factors together. For 20%, 10%, and 5%: 0.80 × 0.90 × 0.95 = 0.684, so you pay 68.4% of the original — a real 31.6% combined discount. Run the calculator twice to chain three.

faq.q: Should the discount be applied before or after tax?
faq.a: Discounts apply to the pre-tax price; sales tax is then calculated on the discounted amount. A bigger discount slightly lowers the tax too. This calculator shows the pre-tax final price.
$200 × 0.85 = $170. You save $30. Common reference: 10% of any price is just move the decimal (10% of $200 = $20), then 15% = $20 + $10 = $30 off.

faq.q: How do retailers use discount math?
faq.a: To hit a target final price: discount % = (1 − targetPrice/originalPrice) × 100. Knowing stacked discounts compound helps avoid giving away more margin than intended when combining a sale with a promo code.
